use_cases.name: Connect a client AI environment through the governed MCP tool surface
use_cases.goal: Let a client's own AI assistant call Nucleus Suite tools with exactly the permissions, approvals and ledger recording that apply to internal agents and human users.

stakeholders.interest: No data leaves the tenant beyond the scopes granted to the calling identity, and every call is auditable.
Their assistant can use HR tools without a separate integration or a parallel permission model.
An external assistant cannot see or change their record unless a permitted person asked it to.

use_cases.trigger: The client wants its enterprise AI assistant to read leave balances and draft letters for HR staff at Vindhya Precision Industries.
preconditions: The tenant has the MCP connection capability enabled and a service identity registered for the client AI environment.
Each tool on the governed tool surface carries a permission scope, a side-effect class and an approval threshold.
The calling human is authenticated through the client identity provider and mapped to a Nucleus principal.
postconditions_success: The client AI environment can list and call only the tools allowed for the connection and for the calling person.
Every call, its inputs, the policy decision and the outcome are written to the action ledger under both the service identity and the human principal.
postconditions_failure: No tool is exposed and the connection stays disabled.
Rejected calls are recorded in the action ledger with the reason.

main_flow.action: Registers the client AI environment as a connection and selects the tools to expose: read_employee, apply_leave and draft_letter.
Shows each tool's permission scope, side-effect class and approval threshold, and blocks tools whose class exceeds the connection ceiling.
Approves the connection through the approval engine after reviewing the exposed tools.
Lists the available tools for the signed-in HR user and receives only those the user's role and data scope allow.
Calls read_employee for E1043 on behalf of the HR user.
Evaluates the call at the policy gate against the user's scope, returns masked fields as masked, and writes the call to the action ledger.
Calls draft_letter for a salary certificate; the platform returns a draft for human review because the tool is write-class.
Reviews the draft in Nucleus Suite and confirms issue; the ledger links the confirmation to the original tool call.

alternate_flows.condition: The call is for an employee outside the HR user's data scope.
steps: The policy gate denies the call.
The client AI environment receives a refusal naming the scope rule, without any employee data.
alternate_flows.rejoin: Use case ends for that call

alternate_flows.condition: The tool's side-effect class is above the connection's approval threshold.
steps: The platform creates an approval request instead of executing.
The call result tells the client AI environment that a human decision is pending.

exception_flows.condition: The service identity's credential has expired or been revoked.
exception_flows.handling: The connection is refused, no tools are listed and the tenant admin is notified.

exception_flows.condition: The call rate exceeds the connection's quota.
exception_flows.handling: The platform throttles further calls, returns a retry-after value and records the event.

nfrs: A permitted read tool call returns within 2 seconds at p95 excluding the client's own processing time.
No tool exposed through MCP bypasses the policy gate; verified by a property test on every build.

user_stories.want: to expose only selected tools to our enterprise AI assistant
user_stories.so_that: the assistant can help HR staff without any wider access than our own users have

acceptance.given: the connection exposes read_employee, apply_leave and draft_letter
acceptance.when: the assistant lists tools for an HR user at LOC-PUN
acceptance.then: exactly those three tools are returned and each shows its permission scope

acceptance.given: a tool is classified above the connection's ceiling
acceptance.when: I try to add it to the connection
acceptance.then: the platform blocks it and names the ceiling

user_stories.want: every external AI tool call recorded with both the service identity and the human on whose behalf it ran
user_stories.so_that: I can answer any access question from the ledger

acceptance.given: the assistant reads E1043's record for an HR user
acceptance.then: the entry shows the connection, the HR user, the tool, the policy decision and that masked fields stayed masked

acceptance.given: the assistant requests an employee outside the HR user's scope
acceptance.then: it is refused, no data is returned and the refusal is in the ledger
